From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit metrics and short checklist

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I attached a lean MAP draft and a unit-metrics workbook so your FinOps folks can drop numbers in. Quick summary here so you have something to share right away:

1) Baseline tokens/$ calc (examples):
  - single-turn summarization (avg tokens in=120, out=60) => ~180 tokens per call
  - streaming chat (avg tokens in=60, incremental out=90) => ~150 tokens per reply
  - placeholder price used: 0.0008 $/token for the curated model family (we'll pin an exact SKU in the MAP)
  - tokens per dollar = 1 / 0.0008 = ~1,250 tokens/$ (back-of-envelope)

2) Batching recommendations (interactive vs batch):
  - interactive: keep batch size = 1–4; batching beyond that adds queuing latency and hurts UX
  - inference-level microbatching (server-side) can pack small concurrent requests without increasing client-visible latency — this is the default on Dedicated

3) Prefetch / caching guidance:
  - prefix caching for repeated system prompts and common completions can reduce token spend by ~10–25% depending on hit rate
  - suggest running a 2-week prefix-cache pilot to estimate hit rate; workbook includes a cache-hit slider

4) Pilot simulation: workbook has two tabs — conservative / optimistic. Inputs we used: traffic profile (your sample attached), mean tokens per path, cache hit %, batching uplift.

Attachments: veridian_map_unitmetrics.xlsx (MAP draft + workbook), prefetch_sim_results.csv (quick sims I ran with your traffic sample)

Next steps: Kimberly will run a short preftech simulation with their SE tooling and I'll update the MAP to include SLA and model SKU callouts. If procurement wants an estimated monthly spend for 10k DAU I can produce an export for them by Tuesday 07/14.

—Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: veridian_map_unitmetrics.xlsx]

Samir — quick follow from SE side with a couple practical checks we recommend during the eval:

Short checklist (SE runbook) — aim for these during a 2-week eval:
- Capture per-path token distributions (not just averages) — 90th percentile matters for cost spikes
- Measure cache hit rate by endpoint (system prompt vs completion cache)
- Run a controlled microbatch experiment: 0, 2, 4, 8 concurrency points and measure p99 latency and cost per token
- Validate streaming vs non-streaming tokenization overhead for your longest chat flows

Prefetch sim notes:
- I ran your sample through a 10k-user synthetic and attached the CSV. Under a 20% cache hit the tokens/$ improved ~14% with no user-visible latency change. At 45% hit we saw >28% improvement but that requires more aggressive prefix normalization on the client side.

If Ben from procurement needs a single-line justification for higher up: "Prefetch + caching reduced expected per-session token consumption in the pilot by 14–28% in synthetic tests, improving tokens/$ materially while preserving latency SLOs."

I'll be available for a 30m call Wed if you want us to walk your engineers through the microbatch script and the workbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prefetch_sim_results.csv]
